subject: Literacy
title: Show what we know
objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
content: Revising listening and sound games, rhymes and books, and words and names through play stations and gathering Term 1 evidence.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and playful; observe quietly and record without interrupting; offer help only when a child is stuck; celebrate what each child can do.
learnerActivities: Show what they know about listening, rhymes, books, words and names through play.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 1 literacy learning using the four-level scale.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with confidence at play stations.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: family and animals

lessons.title: Revising listening
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit listening, loud and quiet, and guess the sound games.
successCriteria: Points to or names a sound source
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, sounds, rhymes, books, words, names and a story this term.
resources: A bell, a rattle, a drum
lessons.starter: Whisper "Shh, listen" and ring the bell. Say "Today we play our favourite sound games."
teacherActivities: Play listening statues with the bell.
Play loud and quiet with the drum.
Play guess the sound with the cloth bag.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
learnerActivities: Children stop and listen on the signal.
Children point to the matching picture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play listening statues with the bell. Children: Children stop and listen on the signal.
Step 2. Teacher: Play loud and quiet with the drum. Children: Children match loud and quiet.
Step 3. Teacher: Play guess the sound with the cloth bag. Children: Children point to the matching picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Sound games
steps: Children play each game for four minutes.
The teacher notes who stops and listens.
practical.safety: Keep sounds gentle and the floor clear. Stop a game if a child covers their ears.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use one sound.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game for friends.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is it loud or quiet?
questions.expected: Child answers by word or action.

expectedOutcomes: Names or points to sound sources
lessons.conclusion: Ring the bell once and whisper "Good listening."
lessons.homeConnection: Play a listening game at home and ask your child to point to the sound.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit listening, loud and quiet, and guess the sound games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising rhymes and books
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit rhymes, songs and picture books.
successCriteria: Holds a book and names a picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, sounds, rhymes, books, words, names and a story this term.
lessons.starter: Sing "Ten little fingers" and say "Let us sing our favourite rhymes."
teacherActivities: Sing two favourite rhymes and pause for the last word.
Look at a book together and ask "What is this?"
Give each child a book to look at.
Let each child choose a rhyme to sing.
learnerActivities: Children join in and fill in the word.
Child holds the book and turns pages.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing two favourite rhymes and pause for the last word. Children: Children join in and fill in the word.
Step 2. Teacher: Look at a book together and ask "What is this?" Children: Child names a picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a book to look at. Children: Child holds the book and turns pages.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a rhyme to sing. Children: Child chooses and sings.

practical.title: Rhyme and book time
steps: Sing a rhyme, then look at a book.
Repeat with a new rhyme and book.
practical.safety: Keep books safe on cushions. Handle books gently and supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Sing with the child and point to the pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a rhyme.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you sing with me?
questions.expected: Child sings or does the actions.

lessons.homeConnection: Sing a rhyme and share a book at home every day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit rhymes, songs and picture books" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising words and names
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will revisit greetings, names, animals and familiar words.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, sounds, rhymes, books, words, names and a story this term.
lessons.starter: Wave and say "Hello, everyone. Let us say hello and name things."
teacherActivities: Play the greeting circle with the puppet.
Hold up name cards and ask "Whose card?"
Show animal pictures and toy foods and ask "What is this?"
Let each child ask for something with please.
learnerActivities: Child asks with a word or phrase.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the greeting circle with the puppet. Children: Children greet each other.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold up name cards and ask "Whose card?" Children: Child finds their card.
Step 3. Teacher: Show animal pictures and toy foods and ask "What is this?" Children: Child names the item.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child ask for something with please. Children: Child asks with a word or phrase.

practical.title: Words circle
steps: Pass a basket of objects and name them.
Greet each friend and say please and thank you.
practical.safety: Use only safe, large objects. Supervise passing and turn-taking.

differentiation.support: Offer two choices and say the word with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name five things.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is your name?
questions.expected: Child says or points to their name.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to each friend by name.
lessons.homeConnection: Name things at home and greet family members with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit greetings, names, animals and familiar words" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Play stations
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 literacy learning at play stations.
successCriteria: Shows listening, speaking and book skills
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, sounds, rhymes, books, words, names and a story this term.
lessons.starter: Sing the hello song and show six stations to the class.
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: listening, rhymes, books, names, animals and story.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: listening, rhymes, books, names, animals and story. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Six stations
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors clear and materials large and soft.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: listens; joins in rhymes; handles a book; names things; greets and responds to name; joins in a story.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Look at the term report and play a favourite game from this term.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 literacy learning at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Term 1 celebration
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 1 with songs, rhymes and a story, and teachers will complete their records.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have worked on listening, sounds, rhymes, books, words, names and a story this term.
resources: A book and a toy goat
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate. Let us sing our favourite songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite rhymes and songs with actions.
Tell the goat story and wait for "munch, munch".
Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name.
learnerActivities: Children join in and choose a song.
Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite rhymes and songs with actions. Children: Children join in and choose a song.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the goat story and wait for "munch, munch". Children: Children join in the story.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or praise and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sing, tell the story and say each name.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing along.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 1 literacy record using today’s observations and the week’s notes. Record a next step for Term 2.

questions.question: Did you like the story?
questions.expected: Yes with a smile or word.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Term 2."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep singing and sharing books during the holiday and say hello to people you meet.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate Term 1 with songs, rhymes and a story, and teachers will complete their records" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
